title: Porcupine Meatballs
subtitle: Beef and rice meatballs simmered in tomato sauce
excerpt: Minced beef mixed with uncooked rice, then simmered in a simple tomato sauce until the rice cooks through and pokes out like spines. An American comfort classic that is very easy to make.
sourceNotes: Mid-20th-century American home cooking; common across the Midwest and South.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze in the sauce. Thaw overnight in the fridge and reheat gently on the hob.
recipe.batchNotes: Double or triple the recipe easily. Use a wide, deep pan so the meatballs sit in a single layer.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The sauce can be made a day ahead. Add the raw meatballs and simmer on the day.

content.text: Porcupine meatballs get their name from the rice grains that poke out through the meat as they cook. The meatballs go into the sauce raw, so the rice inside cooks in the liquid. Keep the simmer very gentle or the meatballs will break apart.
Combine the beef mince, uncooked rice, grated onion, garlic, beaten egg, salt and pepper in a bowl. Mix well with your hands. Roll into balls about the size of a golf ball.
Heat the olive oil in a wide, deep saucepan. Cook the chopped onion for 5 minutes until soft. Add the garlic and paprika. Cook for 1 minute more.
Add the tinned tomatoes, passata and beef stock. Stir well. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Lower the meatballs carefully into the sauce. They should be mostly submerged. Do not crowd the pan.
Cover and simmer very gently for 40 to 45 minutes. Turn the meatballs once, halfway through. The rice grains should be cooked through and poking out of the meat.
Taste the sauce and adjust the seasoning. Serve with the sauce spooned over.

items.symptom: The meatballs break apart in the sauce.
items.cause: The simmer was too vigorous, or the meatballs were turned too early.
items.fix: Keep the heat as low as possible. Wait until the meatballs have firmed up before turning.

items.symptom: The rice is still hard after 45 minutes.
items.cause: The sauce reduced too quickly and there was not enough liquid.
items.fix: Add another 100ml of stock or water, cover again and simmer for a further 15 minutes.

items.cause: The lid was left off during cooking.
items.fix: Keep the lid on for most of the cooking time. Remove it only in the last 5 minutes to thicken.
